answer: Model fingerprinting gives each agent a signature derived from its hardware and weights, and the node resets that signature the moment two identities share a keystroke profile or a funding path. Two boxes on one island rack answering with the same token timing lose their opal badge on match. A farm must vary weights, prompts and timing per account, which is real engineering per clone, and the question is whether a fingerprint costs more than a sparrow's worth of noise.
